properties.statement:
A REBUILD STRANDS AN ATTACHED SESSION'S SHARED SERVER, UNRECOVERABLY, AND THE ERROR POINTS AT A LOG THAT CANNOT EXPLAIN IT. Hit 2026-08-07 doing nothing unusual: `cargo test --workspace` with a Claude Code session attached over MCP. SEQUENCE: the shared daemon reached its 120-minute idle timeout and exited, releasing the store lock — correct, by design, and logged as such. The session's client then tried to auto-start a replacement and failed with "could not spawn the shared reflow2 server: No such file or directory (os error 2)". CAUSE: spawn_daemon resolves the binary with std::env::current_exe() (crates/reflow2-mcp/src/shared.rs). cargo test had relinked reflow2-mcp, so the running process's current_exe() resolved to a DELETED INODE, while a perfectly good binary sat at the same path the whole time. THREE THINGS MAKE IT WORSE THAN A TRANSIENT: (1) it is unrecoverable for the life of the session — every later respawn resolves the same dead inode, and only a full MCP reconnect clears it; (2) the error's advice, "Check the server log beside the graph directory", names the wrong file, because the failure is in the PARENT process and never reaches the daemon log — whose last line is the idle-timeout exit, which reads like the cause and is not; (3) it will hit anyone who runs the test suite while a session is attached, which on this repo is everyone. SAME SHAPE AS fact:defect-lineage-message-omits-its-own-decision: a message whose stated remedy cannot address the actual cause, so the reader spends their time in the wrong place. Note the idle expiry itself is not the defect and should not be 'fixed' — shared.rs documents why the daemon must expire (it holds the store's exclusive write lock, and an immortal daemon trades one lock problem for another).

═══ ADDENDUM 2026-08-12 — FIFTH SIGHTING, AND IT CORRECTS THE RECOVERY STEP ABOVE ═══

Hit again mid-session on 2026-08-12, same mechanism, confirmed by direct measurement rather than inference:
  readlink /proc/341009/exe  -> /home/ajs7/project/reflow2/target/debug/reflow2-mcp (deleted)
  readlink /proc/4067388/exe -> /home/ajs7/project/reflow2/target/debug/reflow2-mcp (deleted)
Both live client processes were executing a deleted inode while a current, executable binary sat at that exact path.

⭐ WHY IT RECURRED DESPITE BEING FIXED, and this is the part worth keeping. The fix landed as `relaunchable_exe_from` in PR #149 (`dafa57f`, "spawn_daemon survives a replaced binary"), merged 2026-08-11. The two client processes started 2026-08-11 at 06:58 and 18:57 — BEFORE that merge. A fix to the spawn path cannot help a session that is already running the binary it fixes: the affected process is by definition the OLD one. ⇒ THE POPULATION THAT HITS THIS DEFECT IS EXACTLY THE POPULATION THE FIX CANNOT REACH, until every long-lived session has been restarted. Confirmed by the error text: the message received was the OLD wording, "could not spawn the shared reflow2 server: No such file or directory (os error 2)", which shared.rs:400 records as the pre-#149 message. The post-fix path names the file it could not find.

🛑 AND IT CORRECTS THE RECOVERY CLAUSE ABOVE. This node says "only a full MCP reconnect clears it". MEASURED FALSE on 2026-08-12: a `/mcp` reconnect does NOT clear it, because a reconnect does not replace a running stdio server — the same process, with the same dead inode, continues serving. Only a FULL RESTART of the client does. The distinction is not pedantic: reconnect is the cheap thing a stranded user will try first, it appears to succeed, and it leaves them exactly as stranded while believing they have already tried the remedy.

WHAT KEPT THE SESSION WORKING: `tools/reflow2_cli.py` spawns its own short-lived process against the store, so every graph write of that afternoon went through it and nothing was lost. Worth knowing — the outage is to the MCP transport, never to the design.
properties.value: {"filed_as":"https://github.com/sligara7/reflow2/issues/91 (finding 2 of 3), 2026-08-07, on Anthony's word","observed":"2026-08-07, cargo test --workspace with an MCP session attached","error":"could not spawn the shared reflow2 server: No such file or directory (os error 2)","cause":"std::env::current_exe() in crates/reflow2-mcp/src/shared.rs spawn_daemon resolves a deleted inode after a relink","binary_was_fine":"target/debug/reflow2-mcp existed and ran throughout","recovery":"full MCP reconnect only","misleading_advice":"'Check the server log beside the graph directory' - failure is in the parent, never reaches that log","blast":"anyone running the test suite with a session attached","not_the_defect":"the 120-minute idle expiry, which shared.rs justifies: the daemon holds the store's exclusive write lock","fix_shape":"fall back to the resolved binary path when current_exe() no longer exists, or detect ENOENT on spawn and name the cause","prior_diagnoses":"recorded in session handoffs 2026-08-06 as 'worth filing and still unfiled'; this is the first time it is in the graph"}
